### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3424eee2ed9f705f37db961494de300c22424606` — the merge of head `27ef04d0d25349fdfef0a9a8c2fd1cca2adb882a` into base `159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3424eee2ed9f705f37db961494de300c22424606 && git checkout 3424eee2ed9f705f37db961494de300c22424606
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549 27ef04d0d25349fdfef0a9a8c2fd1cca2adb882a && git checkout -B drift-repro 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549 && git merge --no-ff 27ef04d0d25349fdfef0a9a8c2fd1cca2adb882a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 159757abc17394bcb0b1240fe382ae3d11a0d549` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dcda950ef927df06ce069bcdff6cd984bca4a70f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + none

PR #34026 (card #33618), net diff against merge base `03b4d2d1f4`. Three files: the ledger (`hits`), `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json` and one changeset. No file in the diff implements or enforces the ledger comment, so the `+` side is empty. The code the comment describes (`packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`) is outside the diff: read at the head, not reviewed. The checklist file and the changeset body are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set: unchanged. Right.** All 18 changed lines of the ledger file (+14 −4) are `//` line comments above the `'OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE'` row. The row, its package key and its neighbours are untouched. No schema, no `.describe()`, no type, no export moves.
- **Public surface: comment bytes only. Right.** `packages/spec/package.json` `files[]` lists `src/**/*.zod.ts`, so the comment ships in the tarball. Nothing a consumer can import or validate against changes.
- **Generated output: none owed. Right.** No generated file is in the diff, and the head's `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Test Core` (8/8) and `TypeScript Type Check` all concluded `success`. No check-run on the head failed; the skipped ones are opt-in, queue-only or UI-path runs.
- **Runtime behaviour: unchanged. Right.** `protocol-handshake.ts` is not in the diff.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/33618-protocol-incompatible-ledger-comment.md` declares `@objectstack/spec: patch`. That matches what the diff publishes: changed bytes in a shipped source file, with no surface change. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`.

Clause-②: no. Held. The PR body, the changeset and the claim all say `no`, and the tree agrees: a comment adds, removes and narrows nothing. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right for the same reason.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Final report (6897707944): `open_questions` is empty.** Nothing to answer.
- **Earlier report (6896248982), Q1 (file-level overlap with #33931 on `platform-core.json`).** Closed by the tree: #33931 is on `main`, the head is a merge of `main` at `03b4d2d1f4`, and the net diff of that file touches one item only (`platform-core.manifest-install-contract`: `acceptance[1]`, `revision` 10 to 11, one history row).
- **Earlier report, Q2 (say `targetMajor` is on every arm, not "instead").** Answered A, and A is what the code does: `checkProtocolCompat` puts `targetMajor` in the diagnostic unconditionally (line 569) and `protocolIncompatibleAnswer` copies it unconditionally (line 252).
- **Flag for the seat, not a finding on the diff.** The final report rests both answers on "the coordinator's two rulings". Card #33618 carries three comments (the claim and the two reports) and no ruling. I judged Q1 and Q2 against the tree, where both hold; the rulings themselves are not on the record I was given.
- **Dev deviations.** The model-free commit trailer, the unrun repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the untested spec dependents are lane matters; CI on the head covers the last two (`Lint · ESLint`, `Test Core`: `success`).
- **Out-of-scope findings (ADR-0087 lines 116, 191, 536 still teach `--from N` / `--from 10`).** Correctly left unedited here. They are "noted, not filed": the seat owns filing them.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`**: every sentence of the rewritten comment, read against `protocol-handshake.ts` and `registry.ts.template` at the head.

Holds:

- "Answered 422": `ProtocolIncompatibleError.status` and `.statusCode` are 422.
- "`requiredRange`, `rangeSource`, `protocolVersion` and `targetMajor` in `error.details` on every refusal": `protocolIncompatibleAnswer` (lines 248 to 254) sets all four unconditionally. `targetMajor` may be `null`, but the member is always there.
- "`--from N` for a `targetMajor` from the migrate-meta support floor up to the runtime's major": lines 527 to 540. The command is withheld when `targetMajor` is above `runtimeMajor` or below `MIGRATE_META_SUPPORT_FLOOR`, so both ends are inclusive, as written.
- "(`MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR`, 16, ADR-0087 D3)": the spec constant is 16 (`registry.ts.template`), the handshake's private copy `MIGRATE_META_SUPPORT_FLOOR` is 16, and `protocol-handshake.test.ts` (line 590) holds the two equal. Naming the spec's constant in the spec's own file is the right choice.
- "the bare `objectstack migrate meta` when `targetMajor` is null": line 540.
- "absent when AHEAD (#26480), where the message names upgrading the runtime or installing a build for this runtime's protocol": lines 541 to 543.
- "absent BELOW the floor (#33466), where `--from N` refuses and the message names installing a build for this runtime's protocol, or bringing the metadata to the floor by another path and then running `--from 16`": lines 544 to 549, and `MigrationFloorError` per the registry's jsdoc.
- Absent means left out, never `undefined`: line 253 and line 570. The comment's "absent" is exact.
- The card's Expected item 1 (name when the command is absent and what the refusal carries instead) is met, and met with the code's facts instead of the card's loose "carries `targetMajor` instead".

Tried to break it: a `||` union with one alternative below the floor (`^15 || ^17` on an 18 runtime) targets 15 and gets no command, which the comment's `targetMajor` wording covers; a `null` target gets the bare command, which the comment says; an empty span yields `null`, same arm. No arm of the code falls outside the comment's four cases.

Findings:

1. **should-fix. "the remedy is a change to the package, not to the environment" is false for the AHEAD arm, and the same comment contradicts it nine lines later.** The sentence is new in this diff (it replaces "the remedy is a body change (`objectstack migrate meta --from N`)"). For a target ahead of the runtime, the first remedy the message names is `Upgrade the runtime to protocol N` (line 543), which is a change to the environment and not to the package; the comment itself then says "the message names upgrading the runtime". A reader is told in one sentence that no environment change resolves the refusal and in another that one does. The sentence is also the comment's stated ground for 422 over 409, so it is the one sentence an agent reads to decide whether resubmitting can ever succeed. The handshake's own jsdoc (lines 151 to 154) words the same rationale without the absolute: the remedy is to change the body, or for a package ahead of the runtime a build of it for this protocol, and 409 is for environment STATE where the same body could succeed later. Fix: drop "not to the environment" and say what the 422 ground really is, for example "the caller's remedy is to send a different body (migrated metadata, or a build for this runtime's protocol); the one remedy outside the body, a runtime upgrade for a package AHEAD, is a deployment change, not environment state". The fix is in the ledger file, so it moves the head and earns a delta review.
2. **nit. "present only when the chain can replay the package's metadata" overstates the `null` arm.** When `targetMajor` is not determinable the code offers the bare command without knowing the chain can replay anything; the diagnostic's own jsdoc says "or is not determinable". The enumerated cases after the colon are right, so no reader is misled about the wire.
3. **nit. The literal `16` appears twice (`..., 16, ADR-0087 D3` and `--from 16`) with nothing to red it when the floor moves.** The handshake's copy is pinned by a test; this comment is not. Naming `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR` beside it limits the harm. Accepted deviation or a follow-up, the dev's choice.

No must-fix. Finding 1 does not change the wire, the accept-set or the `migrateCommand` contract the card is about, so it does not fail the head; it does earn a delta review of its fix.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

### Should-fix 1: fixed

The false sentence ("the remedy is a change to the package, not to the environment") is gone. Its replacement names the runtime upgrade for a package ahead of the runtime, so the passage no longer contradicts the AHEAD sentence lower in the same comment. The 422 ground is now stated as "the same body never succeeds on this runtime", which is the handshake jsdoc's own ground (lines 151 to 157) without the absolute.

### Each sentence checked

Against `checkProtocolCompat` (lines 505 to 574) and `ProtocolIncompatibleError` (lines 179 to 188) at the head.

- **"the manifest is well-formed, but it declares a range this runtime can never satisfy, so the same body never succeeds on this runtime."** True. `checkProtocolCompat` is pure: its verdict depends only on the manifest's declared range and `protocolVersion` (lines 509 to 520). The same manifest on the same runtime reaches `incompatible` every time. "On this runtime" scopes the claim correctly, so it does not collide with the runtime-upgrade remedy that follows.
- **"The remedy is a different body (migrated metadata, or a build for this runtime's protocol), or, for a package ahead of the runtime, a runtime upgrade, which is a deployment change, not environment state."** True, arm by arm:
  - migrated metadata: the default arm, `Run: objectstack migrate meta [--from N]` (lines 538 to 540, 550), and the second half of the below-floor arm (lines 547 to 549).
  - a build for this runtime's protocol: named by the AHEAD arm (line 543) and the below-floor arm (line 547).
  - a runtime upgrade, for a package ahead only: `Upgrade the runtime to protocol N` appears only under `ahead` (lines 541 to 543).
  - "a deployment change, not environment state": consistent with the jsdoc's use of 409 for state "where resubmitting the same body could succeed later" (lines 155 to 157), and with the ledger's own `CONCURRENT_UPDATE` example.
- **"It matches this package's own METADATA_SCHEMA_INVALID. It is not 409, which this ledger keeps for refusals from environment state (CONCURRENT_UPDATE)."** Words unchanged, rewrapped only. `status` and `statusCode` are 422 (lines 181 to 182).
- **"The two HTTP doors that reach the throw, `POST /api/v1/packages` and (since #21805)"**: words unchanged, rewrapped only.

### Did anything else move

No. The word-level diff shows exactly the replaced clause plus comment-marker reflow on four following lines. No schema, `.describe()`, type, export, ledger row or package key changed. The rest of the comment (`migrateCommand` cases, the two `16` literals) is byte-identical to the reviewed head.

### Findings

No must-fix. No should-fix.

1. **nit. "It matches this package's own METADATA_SCHEMA_INVALID" has lost its near antecedent.** "It" meant the 422 answer; it now follows a sentence whose last noun is the runtime upgrade. A reader recovers it from "It is not 409" one sentence on. "The status matches" would be exact.
2. **nit. A `||` union can make a runtime upgrade work for a package the code does not class as ahead.** `^17 || ^19` on an 18 runtime targets 17 (`declaredTargetMajor` takes the lowest alternative, lines 451 to 462), so the message offers `--from 17` and no upgrade, though a move to 19 would also admit it. The comment's "for a package ahead of the runtime" is not false for that case, and it describes what the message names. Noted, no change asked.

Prior nits 2 and 3 (6898175107) are outside the delta and stand as recorded.
